cands.name: Robert T. Reives II
cands.bio: Attorney and partner at Wilson & Reives in Sanford. Former Lee County assistant district attorney. Has served in the North Carolina House for District 54 since January 2014. Elected House Democratic (minority) leader in December 2020.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina (listed as a 2026 endorsement on Ballotpedia).
In 2014, NC State AFL-CIO, Chatham and Lee chapters of the North Carolina Association of Educators, and the Sierra Club (per Ballotpedia).

His campaign site lists endorsements from the North Carolina Association of Educators, NC League of Conservation Voters PAC, State Employees Association of NC, Equality NC and others; it says the AFL-CIO, NCAE and Sierra Club have endorsed him each election.

cands.gaps: I could not find where or in which state Robert Reives was born; Wikipedia gives only his birth date (September 24, 1970). He grew up in Sanford, so no move to North Carolina is documented. I found no record of specific bills he sponsored or deeds in office on any of the ten policy areas, and no statements from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land ownership, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. I found no documented controversies, foreign ties or land-use or data-center stances. The campaign site's bio and news section appear to date from the 2024 cycle, and his 2018 survey answers are the most detailed statements available.

local.label: Roots 90: Wikipedia says he grew up and attended schools in Sanford and graduated from Lee County High School in 1988; his campaign site says he lives in Goldston and represents the families he grew up with in rural North Carolina. His birthplace isn't stated on any page I read.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2014 and has been House Democratic Leader since December 2020, after serving as Deputy Democratic Leader. Earlier he was a Lee County assistant district attorney. He has been a law-firm partner at Wilson & Reives for almost two decades and is a certified mediator. He holds a B.S. in business administration/finance and a J.D., both from UNC-Chapel Hill.
qual.why: More than a decade of legislative service plus chamber leadership, combined with a law career, falls in the top band of the rubric for writing law and the state budget.
